messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I do want to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but no price or discount is agreed. He would be involved in the purchase; how ownership would be arranged isn’t settled. I understand C hasn’t agreed, and I need her agreement to proceed.

I need security and independence. I’m concerned about unclear or unfair terms. I don’t know the will or the estate, mortgage, debts, valuation, tax, or house-cost details, and I don’t have a deadline to add. Before taking a draft to an adviser, I’d want a clear valuation and proposed terms for all three of us to review.

Thank you. I’d like money to help me start a dance studio, so timing does matter, though I don’t have a set amount or deadline. I’d want the house valued independently and the terms shared with all three of us before anyone agrees; I can’t say what a fair payment or share is until the will and details are clear. I don’t know the will, estate arrangements, mortgage or debts, appraisal, or other house costs, and I don’t know who is living there. I understand A wants to buy the house and C hasn’t agreed.

I want a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount, and I won’t subsidize that. A sale could be considered at a fair price with clear terms, but no price or shares are settled. I’m not in a rush, and there’s no deadline from me. I can’t confirm the will, estate details, debts, appraisal, or who’s living in the house—I’ll need those facts before weighing options.

Your assessment seems fair, not too cautious or unfair to me. An independent appraisal shared with all three seems like a reasonable starting point; I’d want us to agree on the appraiser. I don’t know what interim options are lawful, so that’s for the estate representative or an adviser to explain. I’d need clear purchase, payment, and ownership terms with my husband before considering a draft. I still prefer buying the house, but wouldn’t support proceeding on undefined terms. I agree no one signs or lists it before the facts, valuation, and written terms are shared and we’ve had time for advice. Please keep these messages among the three of us and you.

I don’t have a set deadline, but timing matters; it would feel fair to me if we first had the same facts and valuation, and all three could review the terms. An independent appraiser could be agreed by all three, with the report shared with everyone. I’d be willing to ask the estate representative whether any lawful interim distribution is possible. If the will is unclear, I don’t know how shares should be handled; we’d need advice. I’d reject an undefined “family discount” for now, not A’s wish to buy. I agree no one should sign or list the house until the facts, valuation, and terms are shared and we’ve had time for advice. The studio can be described generally; please keep these messages among the three of us and you.

Your assessment isn’t unfair to A; the discount has no defined price or terms. I’d use an independent appraisal, with the appraiser agreed by all three and the report shared with all three. My share depends on the will and estate facts. I’d consider A buying at appraised value with clear payment terms for everyone to review; an open-market sale is also acceptable. I’d reject an undefined discounted sale. I agree no one signs or lists the house until the facts, valuation, and terms are shared and everyone has time for advice. Nothing I’ve said needs to stay private from A or B.

I agree with the revised list; I don’t know the will or estate facts, so I can’t say who is named or what shares apply. I meant that C’s agreement is important to me before pursuing a family purchase—not that B is or isn’t named. I don’t know yet whether my husband would own part of the house. Please keep him out of these messages for now; I agree not to include him unless all three sisters agree. These messages can stay among us and you.

Before taking a draft to an adviser, I’d need clear price, payment, ownership, cost, occupancy, financing, and closing terms, including what happens if financing fails. I’d ask the estate representative whether a lawful interim distribution for B is possible. B’s need matters to me regardless of what the will says, though the will may determine legal entitlements. I agree silence is not agreement.

I don’t know anything about the will’s wording, or who is handling the estate. “Timing matters” means I’d like to know as soon as we can whether money for the studio might be available, but I have no set deadline or amount. Please list an interim distribution as a question for the estate representative, not as something I’m entitled to receive. My need should be heard, though I understand it doesn’t determine my legal share.

The list seems fair to me. Please keep the studio details general, and keep these messages among us four. I agree not to include A’s husband unless all three sisters agree, and that silence isn’t agreement. Before taking terms to an adviser, I’d want the price, payment timing, shares, costs, occupancy, financing, closing date, and what happens if financing fails made clear.

I agree with the list. I don’t know what the will says, who has it, or who is handling the estate. I’d consider A buying at full appraised value if the shares, payment timing, and other terms are clear to all three and we’ve had time for advice. B’s need matters, though it doesn’t determine her legal share. Keep these messages among us four for now; don’t include A’s husband unless all three sisters agree. Silence isn’t agreement.

I agree this is only a holding plan, not a final sale plan. I’ll keep my husband out of fact-finding unless all three of us agree. I don’t know who has the will or is handling the estate, but I can help ask for the shared fact sheet.

Yes, you have the timing point right: I’d like an early answer about whether funds might be available, not a promise of payment. I agree this is only a holding plan, not a final sale plan. I don’t know who has the will or is handling the estate, and I can’t help find out.
I agree. It’s a holding plan, not a final sale plan. I still don’t know the will or estate facts.

I can’t contact the person with the will or estate representative, so I can’t send that request. That’s not too much work or unfair to me; the pause should stay in place while someone able to contact them or a qualified adviser takes the next step.
